To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

taller people live longer and have a lower risk of many diseases, but not all. 7 The findings are consistent across populations and over time and are robust to adjustment, although residual confounding cannot be excluded.

height is a strong predictor of all-cause mortality and of mortality due to most major causes of death, and the association is similar for men and women. 7 The association is independent of socioeconomic position.

(i) taller people are healthier than their shorter counterparts; (ii) taller people live longer; (iii) the association between height, health and longevity is not explained by income and other measures of socio-economic status; (iv) the association between income and health and longevity is partly explained by height; and (v) height is associated with a range of health outcomes.

understanding how the association between height, socioeconomic position, and health is established during early life.
the long and short term effects of early life conditions on health and well-being in adulthood, including the effects of height.
the biological mechanisms that link height with health and mortality.
